notes:
A nested bullet no longer draws at the wrong indent after converting a line into a bullet.

**Fixes & polish**

- **Child bullets always draw at their real depth.** Converting an existing line into a bullet under a parent (toggle-bullet on a line that's already a child) could leave the bullet drawn **flat at the left margin** even though it really was nested — collapsing the parent hid it correctly, but the indent was missing, and Tab couldn't repair it (there was nothing above to nest under, so Tab rightly did nothing). The indent calculation could lose track of a block's parent when the block's identity appeared twice internally; it now always trusts the authoritative copy. Existing affected bullets snap to their correct indent automatically — no data was ever wrong, only the drawing. (PRD Addendum 2 §B; found in the Aug-17 journal.)

**Under the hood**

- The Hierarchy depth scan is now first-occurrence-wins per block id (the outermost node is the authoritative carrier), guaranteed to cause zero content changes and zero spurious sync ops on load. Pinned by unit tests on the exact colliding shape and by both-engine e2e with pixel-geometry asserts (one 24px step per depth level). Also repaired a date-pinned palette test that had begun failing on real-clock drift.
